skeptic.objection: The first pass missed a historic church cemetery on this parcel's north line. In the county parcel map, one part of the Welcome All Road Cemetery parcel (4582 Welcome All Rd SW) shares about 61 m of the lead's north boundary, by my measurement from the county shapes. The cemetery's own association reports that a ground-penetrating-radar survey found over 30 unmarked burials. Georgia law forbids disturbing a known cemetery or burials to develop land without a local permit. The 2026 rewrite of that law (SB 146, as passed) allows a disturbance permit only for an 'abandoned' cemetery, and this one is actively maintained, fenced and mapped. Any graves that extend past the recorded line onto the north tip would therefore have to be avoided. This does not kill the lead, because the wide south end is where a building would fit. Still, a person must settle the cemetery's true edge and any local buffer before relying on the usable-acre and building-fit numbers. Second doubt: the owner is tied by mailing address to the industrial landlord whose built park adjoins on the south. The parcel may be held as that park's own expansion land or yard, not for sale. Nothing found shows it is listed or wanted by anyone else.

claims.text: The county parcel record (queried by parcel id, not by name) shows parcel 09F350101520017 at 4582 Welcome All Rd SW as exempt cemetery land (class E4, land use 601) held by the Welcome All Road Cemetery Preservation Association. By my measurement from the county parcel shapes (a map-box query of layer 11 with geometry returned), one of its two polygon parts, about 0.3 acres, shares about 61 m of the lead parcel's north line. The cemetery's preservation association says a GPS and ground-penetrating-radar mapping of the cemetery (2023) found over 30 unmarked burials. Unmarked graves exist here, and the recorded or fenced line may not be the edge of the burials.

claims.text: The association describes the site as a historic cemetery under active care: restoration, preservation, a survey and a perimeter fence. That is relevant to whether it could ever count as 'abandoned' under the 2026 law (below).
claims.quote: Welcome All Road Cemetery Preservation Association Inc is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit volunteer group of individuals striving for the beautification, restoration, and preservation of historic Welcome All Road Cemetery in South Fulton, Georgia.

claims.text: Georgia DCA's cemetery FAQ (updated 01/01/2025) summarises O.C.G.A. 36-72: a known cemetery or burial may not be disturbed to develop or change the use of land without a permit from the local governing authority.
claims.quote: Provides that no known cemetery or burial object shall be disturbed for purposes of developing or changing the use of that land unless a permit is first obtained from the local governing authority.

claims.text: The same FAQ says state law sets no buffer around a cemetery, but some Georgia cities and counties have local cemetery buffer ordinances. Whether South Fulton has one is not shown (its code is on Municode, a known wall).
claims.quote: Some counties and cities in Georgia have now enacted local ordinances setting out buffers and other requirements a developer must follow when the project area includes a cemetery.

claims.text: 2026 Senate Bill 146, as passed and posted on the Governor's 2026 signed-legislation page, rewrites O.C.G.A. 36-72-4 so that a disturbance permit may be issued only for an 'abandoned cemetery'. The next sentence of the bill, not quoted here, reads 'unless such cemetery or burial ground constitutes an abandoned cemetery as defined in this chapter.' The effective date was not read.

open_items: Commission a ground-penetrating-radar or archaeological check along the lead's north line beside the Welcome All Road Cemetery parcel, and get the cemetery's 2022 boundary survey (the association says Jackson Land Surveying did it). Find out whether any burials lie on 09F350101520306.

Ask City of South Fulton planning (and its Historic and Cultural Landmarks Commission) whether a cemetery buffer or setback applies to development next to 4582 Welcome All Rd SW, and confirm SB 146's effective date and final text.

Ownership of the lead and of the adjoining built park (4677 and 4601 Welcome All Rd) share one New Jersey mailing address. A person should find out, without contacting the owner through this process, whether the lead is held as the park's expansion land, trailer yard or stormwater area. Its zero improvement value does not rule out such a use (hence the dispute of market-3).

Seen, not verifiable: the county parcel shapes put single-family lots (4630 and 4650 Welcome All Rd, 4221 Kenwood Trl, and a residential-class lot at 0 Welcome All Rd) and a church (4590 Will Lee Rd) about 15 to 21 m from the lead's road frontage, i.e. across Welcome All Road, by my measurement. The adopted M-2 buffer rule toward residential use across a street could not be read (Municode). A 2020 draft zoning Article 4 on the city site mentions buffers adjacent to residential zoning but is a draft.

The Aerotropolis CIDs project page for Welcome All Rd (aacids.govocal.com/projects/welcome-all-rd) is JavaScript-only and showed no text. Web search results describe right-of-way purchases to realign Welcome All Road at Camp Creek Parkway, which by map position appears well north of this parcel, but that was not confirmed.

Seen, not verifiable: a third-party meeting summary in search results said the Planning Commission recommended R-5 for Z26-002 despite a staff recommendation of denial. That differs from plans-3's 'both recommended approval'. The council decision of 04/15/2026 is still unread.
